segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My topic is handedness- whether in different sports it is better to be left- or right-sided or whether a more balanced approach is more successful.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I'm left-handed myself and I actually didn't see any relevance to my own life when I happened to start reading an article by a sports psychologist called Peter Matthews.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: He spent the first part of the article talking about handedness in music instead of sport, which I have to say almost put me off from reading further.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But what I soon became struck by was the sheer volume of both observation and investigation he had done in many different sports and I felt persuaded that what he had to say would be of real interest.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I think Matthews' findings will be beneficial, not so much in helping sportspeople to work on their weaker side, but more that they can help them identify the most suitable strategies to use in a given game.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Although most trainers know how important handedness is, at present they are rather reluctant to make use of the insights scientists like Matthews can give, which I think is rather short-sighted because focusing on individual flexibility is only part of the story.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Anyway, back to the article.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Matthews found a German study which looked at what he called 'mixed-handedness', that is, the capacity to use both left and right hands equally.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It looked at mixed-handedness in 40 musicians on a variety of instruments.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Researchers examined a number of variables, e.g. type of instrument played, regularity of practice undertaken and length of time playing instrument . . . and found the following: keyboard players had high levels of mixed- handedness, whereas string players like cellists and violinists strongly favoured one hand.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Also those who started younger were more mixed-handed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Matthews also reports studies of handedness in apes.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Apes get a large proportion of their food by 'fishing' ants from ant hills.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The studies show that apes, like humans, show handedness- though for them right- and left-handedness is about equal, whereas about 85% of humans are right-handed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Studies showed that apes consistently using the same hand fished out 30% more ants than those varying between the two.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Matthews started researching several different sports and found different types of handedness in each.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: By the way, he uses 'handedness' to refer to the dominant side for feet and eyes as well as hands.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Anyway, his team measured the hand, feet and eyes of 2,611 players and found that there were really three main types of laterality: mixed - you work equally well on both sides - both hand and eye; single- you tend to favour one side but both hand and eye favour the same side; and cross-laterality - a player's hands and eyes favour only one side but they are opposite sides.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Let's start with hockey.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Matthews found that it was best to be mixed- handed -this is because a hockey stick must be deployed in two directions - it would be a drawback to have hand or eye favouring one side.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: An interesting finding is that mixed-handed hockey players were significantly more confident than their single-handed counterparts.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Things are slightly different in racket sports like tennis.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Here the important thing is to have the dominant hand and eye on the one side.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This means that there is a bigger area of vision on the side where most of the action occurs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If a player is cross lateral the racket is invisible from the dominant eye for much of the swing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It means that they can only make corrections much later ... and often the damage has been done by then.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And moving to a rather different type of sport which involves large but precise movements- gymnastics.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It's been found that cross hand-eye favouring is best.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The predominant reason for this is because it aids balance- which is of course absolutely central to performance in this sport.
